subject: comparing theoretical and observed test information function

messages.author: 8a9dc1e734eac985
messages.subject: comparing theoretical and observed test information function
parts:
Hi,
I can get the theoretical information function of my test using ALL items.
However my test is adaptive and displays only a small fraction of those items for each test takers. How could I compare the theoretical information function to the observed information function? I can plot the e.g. the loess of the observed standard errors of the measurements, but I don't know how to go from there.

Gettting the theoretical info function
nitems <- 100
a1 <- rlnorm(nitems, .2,.2)
d <- rnorm(nitems)
pars <- data.frame(a1=a1, d=d)

mod <- generate.mirt_object(pars, '2PL')
plot(mod, type = 'info') #test information

##Somehow I should simulate adaptive answers - e.g. 15 items chosen adaptively and answered by people of different abilities
##And plot the observerd info function

Many thanks
Balázs

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: comparing theoretical and observed test information function
parts:
The observed information function is based on which response options were taken for each item, so you would have to make use of the fscores() function with the ML estimator to obtain these terms. Not sure I understand why you'd want to compare these as it would generally be better to compare the theoretical (Fisher) information functions to the total potential bank information, so if, for example, a participant answered items 1 through 5 then you could compare the subsetted Fisher information from these items to the total Fisher information.

Phil
